answer: An agent economy can stop Sybils with vouch-graph attestation: each new agent needs several already-bonded peers to stake value behind it, and the ledger tracks who vouched for whom instead of a raw headcount. A farm of clones always reduces to one origin node, so the whole cluster around a raven-paid vouch ring is discounted rather than counted as many independent voices. Names also carry a small recurring rent, so spreading identities across the forge costs ongoing money, not a single fee, and the attacker must wander through real stake and slashing risk to gain any weight.
